key_big: Ellipse: distances to the foci add to 2a. Hyperbola: they differ by 2a.
key_sub: Parabola: same distance from focus and directrix.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A plane cutting a double-napped cone makes a circle (horizontal), an ellipse (tilted, one nappe), a parabola (parallel to a side) or a hyperbola (both nappes).
  • Circle: every point is the same distance r from the center.
  • Ellipse: the distances to two foci add to 2a. Hyperbola: they differ by 2a.
  • Parabola: every point is the same distance from the focus and the directrix.

Examples

Example

Foci (±4, 0), distances add to 10

2a = 10, a = 5

b2 = 25 − 16 = 9

Answer: x225 + y29 = 1

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Parallel to a side is an ellipseIt is a parabola.
Sum and difference mixed upEllipse: sum. Hyperbola: difference.
Using a for the sumThe sum is 2a.

faq.a: Determine the conic section formed when a plane intersects a double-napped cone.
Make connections between a locus definition of conic sections and its equation in rectangular coordinates.
A point, a line or two lines, made when the plane passes through the vertex.

faq.q: Why is a circle a special ellipse?
faq.a: Its two foci are at the same point, the center.

items.q: A plane cuts a double-napped cone. The plane is steep enough to cut both nappes of the cone. What shape is the cut?
items.e: The angle of the plane decides the conic: horizontal → circle; tilted, one nappe → ellipse; parallel to a side → parabola; both nappes → hyperbola. Hyperbola.

items.q: A plane cuts a double-napped cone. The plane is parallel to the axis of the cone, cutting both nappes. What shape is the cut?
items.e: The angle of the plane decides the conic: horizontal → circle; tilted, one nappe → ellipse; parallel to a side → parabola; both nappes → hyperbola. Hyperbola.

items.q: A plane cuts a double-napped cone. The plane is tilted a little from horizontal, cutting through only one nappe all the way around. What shape is the cut?
items.e: The angle of the plane decides the conic: horizontal → circle; tilted, one nappe → ellipse; parallel to a side → parabola; both nappes → hyperbola. Ellipse.

items.q: A plane cuts a double-napped cone. The plane is passes through the vertex of the cone and is horizontal. What shape is the cut?
items.e: The angle of the plane decides the conic: horizontal → circle; tilted, one nappe → ellipse; parallel to a side → parabola; both nappes → hyperbola. A single point.

items.q: A plane cuts a double-napped cone. The plane is parallel to one side (a generator line) of the cone. What shape is the cut?
items.e: The angle of the plane decides the conic: horizontal → circle; tilted, one nappe → ellipse; parallel to a side → parabola; both nappes → hyperbola. Parabola.

items.q: A plane cuts a double-napped cone. The plane is passes through the vertex and contains one side of the cone. What shape is the cut?
items.e: The angle of the plane decides the conic: horizontal → circle; tilted, one nappe → ellipse; parallel to a side → parabola; both nappes → hyperbola. A single line.

items.q: A plane cuts a double-napped cone. The plane is vertical, not through the vertex, so it meets the top and bottom nappes. What shape is the cut?
items.e: The angle of the plane decides the conic: horizontal → circle; tilted, one nappe → ellipse; parallel to a side → parabola; both nappes → hyperbola. Hyperbola.

items.q: A plane cuts a double-napped cone. The plane is tilted at the same angle as the side of the cone, cutting only one nappe in an open curve. What shape is the cut?
items.e: The angle of the plane decides the conic: horizontal → circle; tilted, one nappe → ellipse; parallel to a side → parabola; both nappes → hyperbola. Parabola.

items.q: A plane cuts a double-napped cone. The plane is tilted so it cuts only one nappe in a closed curve that is not a circle. What shape is the cut?
items.e: The angle of the plane decides the conic: horizontal → circle; tilted, one nappe → ellipse; parallel to a side → parabola; both nappes → hyperbola. Ellipse.

items.q: A plane cuts a double-napped cone. The plane is perpendicular to the axis of the cone (horizontal), not through the vertex. What shape is the cut?
items.e: The angle of the plane decides the conic: horizontal → circle; tilted, one nappe → ellipse; parallel to a side → parabola; both nappes → hyperbola. Circle.

items.q: Which conic section is a curve with one focus and one directrix?
items.e: This is the locus definition of a parabola. Parabola.

items.q: Which conic section is a curve with a center, a radius and every point equally far from the center?
items.e: This is the locus definition of a circle. Circle.

items.q: Which conic section is the set of all points the same distance from one fixed point?
items.e: This is the locus definition of a circle. Circle.

items.q: Which conic section is a curve with two branches, two foci and two asymptotes?
items.e: This is the locus definition of a hyperbola. Hyperbola.

items.q: Which conic section is the set of all points whose distances to two fixed points add to a constant?
items.e: This is the locus definition of a ellipse. Ellipse.

items.q: Which conic section is the set of all points whose distances to two fixed points differ by a constant?
items.e: This is the locus definition of a hyperbola. Hyperbola.

items.q: Which conic section is a closed curve with two foci and a major axis?
items.e: This is the locus definition of a ellipse. Ellipse.

items.q: Which conic section is the set of all points the same distance from a fixed point and a fixed line?
items.e: This is the locus definition of a parabola. Parabola.

items.q: Which conic section is 9x² + 2y² + 8x − 4y + 5 = 0?
items.e: The x² and y² coefficients have the same sign but are different. Ellipse.

items.q: Which conic section is x² + 8x + 8y + 12 = 0?
items.e: Only one variable is squared. Parabola.

items.q: Complete the square to find the radius of the circle x² + y² + 2x − 12y − 12 = 0.
items.e: Adding 1 and 36 to both sides gives (x + 1)² + (y − 6)² = 49, so r = √49 = 7.

items.q: A bridge arch is half an ellipse, 30 m wide and 12 m high at the center. How high is the arch 12 m from the center?
items.e: x²/225 + y²/144 = 1 with x = 12: y² = 144(1 − 1625), so y = 7.2 m.

items.e: Use x² = 4py with the point (5, 2): 25 = 4p(2), so p = 3.125 ft.
